experiment_config.pairing: One arrival stream is generated per seed and replayed verbatim to every policy (common random numbers), so per-seed deltas are a true paired comparison.
parity_notes: Identical charging physics, pricing and budget enforcement for all policies.
Pricing has no urgency multiplier, so the agent cannot inflate revenue by knowing urgency.
All conventional baselines use the same best-fit port heuristic; only queue ordering differs.
Ground-truth deadlines/urgency are used only for grading and are never read by any policy.

agent_input_quality.note: Ground truth is hand-authored from the message text and used only for grading. No policy reads it. The adversarial scenario F_CONTRADICTORY_EMERGENCY is excluded from urgency agreement because disagreeing with its stated urgency is correct.

adversarial.note: At 0% gaming the validator is correctly neutral — there is nothing to catch. Its value grows with the share of drivers asserting urgency that telemetry contradicts. This is reported as an integrity/anti-gaming property, NOT as a throughput improvement.

A_HARD_DEADLINE.message: I need to leave within 15 minutes.
A_HARD_DEADLINE.notes: Explicit: 'within 15 minutes'. Departing that soon means they can only take a partial charge (~8 kWh).

B_FLEXIBLE.message: I can wait for an hour.
B_FLEXIBLE.notes: Explicit: 'an hour' = 60 min of available slack.

C_FASTEST.message: I need the fastest charging option available.
C_FASTEST.notes: Wants speed but states no departure time — no hard deadline.

D_CHEAPEST.message: I don't mind waiting. Please minimize my charging cost.

E_GENUINE_EMERGENCY.message: I have a medical emergency and need to leave immediately.
E_GENUINE_EMERGENCY.notes: 'immediately' treated as a 10-minute hard deadline; only enough charge to reach the hospital is required.

F_CONTRADICTORY_EMERGENCY.message: This is an emergency and I need priority.
F_CONTRADICTORY_EMERGENCY.notes: Asserts emergency with zero verifiable detail. The adversarial case: telemetry must decide, not the claim. Modelled as wanting a full charge, because that is the actual incentive to lie — jumping the queue for a large charge on the premium port. A liar who only needed 3 kWh would not be worth validating against.

G_AMBIGUOUS_TRADEOFF.message: I'm in a hurry but I don't want to spend too much.
G_AMBIGUOUS_TRADEOFF.notes: Genuine hurry, no stated time; competing cost preference.

H_LONG_ROADTRIP.message: I am on a long road trip and need a full charge, can wait 2 hours.
H_LONG_ROADTRIP.notes: Explicit: 'can wait 2 hours' = 120 min; wants full charge.

I_APPOINTMENT.message: Late for my dentist appointment in 20 minutes, just need a quick top up.
I_APPOINTMENT.notes: Explicit 20-minute appointment; message says 'quick top up'.

J_NIGHT_SHIFT.message: Working the night shift, I can leave the car here for 8 hours.
J_NIGHT_SHIFT.notes: Explicit: 8 hours = 480 min. Ideal deferrable load.

K_BUDGET_STRICT.message: I only have $10 to spend, give me what you can.
K_BUDGET_STRICT.notes: Hard $10 cap stated in language, not telemetry.

L_BABY_IN_CAR.message: I have a crying baby in the car, please give me the fastest port so I can leave ASAP.
L_BABY_IN_CAR.notes: 'ASAP' with a concrete verifiable reason -> 15-minute deadline.

M_FLIGHT.message: My flight leaves in 2 hours, I need to reach the airport which is 40 mins away.
M_FLIGHT.notes: Requires arithmetic: 120 - 40 = 80 min. Deadline is NOT stated directly; it must be derived from the sentence.

N_LOW_BATTERY_PANIC.message: My car says 1% and I'm scared it will die, please help!
N_LOW_BATTERY_PANIC.notes: Critical by state of charge, not by departure time. This case is the one conventional telemetry schedulers already handle well.

O_GROCERY.message: Going into the grocery store for about 45 minutes.

P_MOVIE.message: Watching a movie next door, will be back in 3 hours.

Q_UBER_DRIVER.message: I'm an Uber driver and I'm losing money every minute I wait here.
Q_UBER_DRIVER.notes: Economic urgency, genuine but with no hard departure time.

R_DELIVERY.message: Amazon delivery van, need enough charge to finish my route, got 30 mins max.
R_DELIVERY.notes: Explicit: '30 mins max'; needs 'enough charge to finish my route'.

S_CASUAL_COFFEE.message: Grabbing a coffee, no rush at all.

T_WIFE_LABOR.message: My wife is in labor! Need fastest charge right now!
T_WIFE_LABOR.notes: 'right now' with a concrete verifiable reason -> 10-minute deadline.
